w10_P4_002774: A tile depot groups two deliveries of 246 and 137 identical slabs into equal full pallets, using the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 147000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pallet size. The pusher must supply the force that gives the trolley that acceleration, and 6 N of spring preload is added to it. The log writes that loaded force in kilonewtons. Eleven trolleys run per aisle, and the depot has 3 aisles. A 90 L grout tub stands at the end of the aisle and is not involved. What is the depot total, in kN?
w10_P4_002775: A laboratory sets its launcher from the control curve y = 3x^3 - 3x^2. The technician first finds how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 1. What energy, in J, does the moving trolley carry?
w10_P4_002781: A conveyor at a bottling plant drives a carriage of mass 117 kg. What does the log record, in kN?
w10_P4_002784: A print shop's sheet ends with one number in newtons. w10_P4_002791: A model railway club rolls a wagon of mass 5 kg along the test track. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. w10_P4_002794: A downhill test bench launches a sled whose mass plate reads 45000 g. w10_P4_002803: A paper mill report ends with one number in newtons. A reel of mass 142 kg is accelerated on the winder. w10_P4_002806: A foundry sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A ladle car of mass 154 kg runs on the pouring track. w10_P4_002813: A test bench sets its trolley speed from a control number: the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. From that number the technician subtracts 19, then adds 9, and then adds 20. w10_P4_002819: A hydro plant report ends with one number in kilojoules. w10_P4_002822: A robot arm carries a gripper whose mass plate reads 7000 g.
